transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. I'm here to help. What's been going on that brought you in today?
I've just been feeling incredibly down and sad lately. Honestly, I've felt this deep emptiness inside for about the last six months, and it just doesn't seem to go away.
Have you had similar periods of low mood before the last six months, going back further than that?
No, I've never experienced a low mood like this before these past six months. This is really the first time I've ever felt this way, and it's completely new to me.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in most activities you used to enjoy?
Yes, I've completely lost interest in the things I used to love, like gardening and reading. Nothing brings me any happiness or pleasure anymore. It all just feels completely empty and pointless.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently?
I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my appetite or my weight recently. Everything seems to be about the same as usual in that regard.
Have you been having trouble with your sleep—like difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping too much?
I haven't really had any significant issues with my sleep lately. It has been relatively normal, and I'm not having trouble falling asleep or sleeping too much.
Have you been feeling worse about yourself lately, like you're overly critical, guilty, or worthless?
No, I haven't really been feeling excessively guilty, self-critical, or worthless lately. It's more of just a deep emptiness and sadness, rather than feeling bad about myself in that way.
Have you had periods of low mood that lasted for at least two years, even if they felt less severe at times?
No, I've never had a low mood that lasted for that long. This all really just started about six months ago, and it has been constant since then.

The patient meets criteria for depressed mood, anhedonia, and duration (more than two weeks), without significant changes in appetite, sleep, or self-worth, which supports Major Depressive Disorder. No features of mania, psychosis, anxiety disorders, or trauma-related symptoms have been reported. Thus, the only remaining candidate is Major Depressive Disorder.
